correctness.rationale: The proof establishes a unique-palindrome occurrence center for every run and that at a given length at most one palindrome from any center exists. Disjoint run supports rule out a third answer at at most four runs and a fourth at five. If centers 2 and 4 overlap, equality of lengths forces either duplicate strings or a shorter unique middle palindrome \(1 0^c1\). A triple is therefore centered at runs 1,2,3 after symmetry. Explicit run-length constraints imply \(b=d\), \(v=e+1\), \(c\ge v\), \(v\ge b+2\), and hence \(n\ge7b+7\ge14\). Equality fixes a unique run composition. A separate check establishes three distinct length-\(a\) unique palindromes in every explicit parameter-family member and eliminates shorter unique answers. The verifier independently enumerates all 6944 words with at most five runs through length 14 for all intervals and checks 48 family members and 2400 additional intervals. All finite and symbolic obligations are explicitly separated.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new argument excludes centers 2 and 4 as simultaneous shortest answers via a shorter unique palindrome spanning the central run, then forces the outer/adjacent/central pattern and the inequalities \(v=e+1\), \(c\ge v\), \(v\ge b+2\). originality.rationale: Three highly relevant primary texts were inspected with special attention to exact definitions and implication coverage. The previously known bound is four answers for all strings, and RLE SUPS algorithms do not imply the sharper low-run multiplicity hierarchy or first occurrence at length 14. Semantic searches for the same parameter, run-center equivalences and exact witness classification found no equivalent/dominating result. This supports an originality assessment relative to inspected material, while indexing gaps and inaccessible equivalences remain a real residual risk.
residual_risks: A specialization of a stronger theorem may appear in inaccessible or unindexed SUPS literature; searches do not establish historical uniqueness.
The closest general algorithms could be specialized in unpublished work to recover the same thresholds; no such implication was found in inspected primary text.

value.rationale: The number of simultaneous SUPS answers is an algorithmically meaningful natural invariant (it is the output parameter of known SUPS query data structures), and maximal constant runs are a standard compressed-string structural parameter. The theorem sharpens the global upper bound four to two and three on nontrivial infinite run-restricted classes, identifies the first run count at which three answers are possible, proves the exact first witness length and symmetry classification, and supplies an infinite two-parameter family; these are structural classification and tight boundary results, not arbitrary small numerical increments.
